summary: Two unrelated things the group talks about on the same day are now two notes. Until this, anything the background pass wrote for a day it already had a note for was folded into that note, whatever it was about.
details: The note-candidates pass matched a proposed note to a standing one on the ANCHOR DATE alone. Measured 2026-09-13: that arm had fired exactly twice since the tier shipped and both times it merged two genuinely different occasions — a sign-up deadline and a games thread that shared nothing but the calendar day, and a gathering note overwritten forty minutes later by an unrelated room's pass. Notes are per-group, so every room in a group wrote onto whichever note shared the date (issue #228).

The pass is now asked which entry it is updating, and answers with that entry's title exactly as its notebook shows it. Code resolves the title and nothing else: one match revises, nothing named creates, and a title that answers to more than one entry creates rather than guessing which was meant — a duplicate is something the group can see and fix, appending to the wrong entry is not. The date is back to meaning only when the thing happens, which is what schedules the note's own follow-up.

The pass could already see the notebook and was already told not to duplicate what was in it; its answer was being discarded. What changed is that a wrong answer is now recoverable: since the first half of this issue a revision appends rather than replaces, so the worst case is an entry that carries two threads and the group can still read both.
limitations: Two arrangements on one date that the pass proposes WITHOUT naming any people for either are still handled as one — the staging table that queues proposals keys on the date and the people, and with no people named the two collide before the new rule is reached. The pass is now told to name the people whenever one batch gives it two entries on one date.
Resolution is by exact title, so an entry whose title the pass mistypes reads as new and is written as a second entry.
